label: theorem1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem1}
The following conditions characterize a $PT_{K}(V)$ with one added vertex $O$ having $m$ edges issuing from $O,$ (except $m=2,$ where $O$ coincides with one vertex frome the vertex set of three vertices):

A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system)

(B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree).

(C) If $m=3,$ there exists a Platonic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ and the Steiner point is identical with the Fermat point, having three edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ (Hexagonal coordinate system).

(D) If $m$ is even and $m \ge 4,$  there exists a Platonic geodesic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ having $m$ edges , which form platonic angles with only two distinct measures $90^{o}$ and $180^{\circ}.$
(Existence of a Cartesian coordinate system).

(E) If $m\ge 4$, there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ having $m$ edges , which form only platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$
(Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system).



(F) If $m\ge 3,$ there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree $PT_{K}(V)$ having $m$ edges, which form platonic angles with only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system).
head: environment

label: eqone
title: Proof
body_md:
(A)
Let $e_{i}=\frac{\vec{OA_{i}}}{| OA_{i} |}$ be a unit direction tangent vector of the ray $l_{i}$ at $O,$ for $i=1,2,\ldots, m.$ $O$ is the Fermat point having $m$ connections with the geodesic segments $OA_{i}.$ Hence, we have the balancing condition of $e_{i}$ at $O:$

\begin{equation}\label{eqone}
\sum_{i=1}^{m}e_{i}=\vec{0}.
\end{equation}
By squaring both parts of (\ref{eqone}), we need to set $m$ angles with measure $120^{\circ}$ and the rest $\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m$ angles with measure $90^{\circ}.$


Let $\{ \cos \angle A_{i}O A_{j} \}$ be the cosine matrix of the angles $\angle A_{i} O A_{j},$ for $i,j=1,2,\ldots, m.$
We set $\cos \angle A_{i}OA_{i}=1,$  for $i=1,2,\ldots, m,$ \[\angle A_{j} O A_{j+1}=\angle A_{j+1} O A_{j}=120^{\circ},\] for $j=1,2,3,\ldots, m-1,$ which yields \[\cos \angle A_{j} O A_{j+1}=\cos \angle A_{j+1} O A_{j}=-\frac{1}{2}.\]

We set \[\angle A_{1}O A_{m}=\angle A_{m}OA_{1}=120^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{1} O A_{m}=\cos \angle A_{m} O A_{1}= -\frac{1}{2}.\]

We set the rest $\frac{m(m-1)}{2} - m$ angles \[\angle A_{i} O A_{j} =90^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{i}O A_{j}=0,\] for $i<j.$
Hence, we get \[\angle A_{j} O A_{i} =90^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{j}O A_{i}=0.\]
By following this construction, we get exactly two elements of the cosine matrix with value $-\frac{1}{2}$ one with value $1$ and the rest with value $0.$
in each row and each column.

These values satisfy the following combinatorial system of equations of unit tangent vectors $e_{i}$ at $O,$ derived by (\ref{eqone}):

\[-e_{i_{1}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne i_{1} }^{m} e_{i},\]
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}-e_{i_{3}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2},i_{3}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
$\cdots$
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}-\ldots-e_{i_{k}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2},i_{3},\ldots, i_{k}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
for $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots, i_{k} \in \{1,2,\ldots, m\}$ and $k<\frac{m}{2}.$


(B)  $m=2$ Two geodesic segments $A_{1}A_{2}$ and $A_{2}A_{3}$ (or rays in $H_{K}^{2}$), which meet at angle $\angle A_{1}A_{2}A_{3}=120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ gives a minimum spanning tree $MST_{K}( \{ A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3} \} )  )$ and $O=A_{2}$ is the Fermat point (degenerate Fermat tree or Steiner tree), which coincides with a $PT_{K}(\{ A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3} \}).$

(C) For $m=3,$ consider a vertex set of three vertices, which form a geodesic triangle with angles $120^{\circ}-\epsilon,$ where $\epsilon$ is a positive real number. Hence, we get $e_{1}+e_{2}+e_{3}=\vec{0},$ such that: $\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{2}=\angle A_{2}A_{0}A_{3}=\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{3}=120^{\circ}$ and $PT_{K}(\{ A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3} \})=MST_{K}(\{ A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3} \})$ with one added vertex $O$ (Fermat point or Steiner point).

(D) For $m$ even, we get an $\frac{m}{2}$ orthoplex having $m$ vertices and $\frac{m}{2}$ diagonals, which meet at a right angle. Hence, the edges of the geodesic tree form $m (\frac{m}{2}-1)$ right angles and $\frac{m}{2}$ straight angles, which yields a $PT_{K}(V)$.

(E) For $m\ge 4,$ we assume that $\frac{m(m-1)}{2}$ $\angle A_{i}O A_{j}$  have measure $120^{\circ}$ for $i,j=1,2, \ldots, m$ and $ i<j.$ By squaring both parts of the balancing condition of $e_{i}$ in(\ref{eqone}), we obtain:
\[ m - \frac{m (m-1) }{2} = 0 ,\]

 which gives $m=3 <4 .$
Therefore, there does not exist a $PT_{K}(V)$ with $\frac{m(m-1)}{2}$ angles with measure $120^{\circ}$ for $m\ge 4.$

(F) For $m\ge 3,$ we assume that there is at least one angle $\angle A_{i}OA_{j}$ with measure $150^{\circ}.$ By squaring both parts of the balancing condition of $e_{i}$ in(\ref{eqone}), we obtain that the irrational number $m +a + b\sqrt{3}=0,$ for $a,b$ real numbers. Hence, there does not exist a $PT_{K}(V),$ such that each two incident edges meet at an angle having only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}.$

label: theorem2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem2}
If an $IT_{K}(V)$ has $m$ boundary vertices with upto $m-2$ added vertices that lie on their convex geodesic hull and the geodesic rays formed by the edges of this geodesic tree give a Fermat Coordinate System and/or Cartesian Coordinate System and/or Hexagonal coordinate system, then $IT_{K}(V)=PT_{K}(V).$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let an intermediate geodesic tree $IT_{K}(V)$ with $m$ boundary vertices and an added set of vertices $Q,$ which contains upto $m-2$ vertices in the $K-$space. Each point $S_{i}$ in $Q$ may have $k_{i},$ for $i=1,2,\ldots, m-2$ and refers to the conditions of (A), (B), (C), (D) of Theorem~\ref{theorem1}. There might be some vertices of the original vertex set $V$ that fullfill case (B) of Theorem~1. Hence, we get: $IT_{K}(V)=PT_{K}(V).$

label: propthree
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{propthree}
If $m$ is even, such that: $\angle A_{j} O A_{j+2}=\angle A_{1} O A_{m}=\angle A_{2}OA_{m-1}=120^{\circ},$ for $j=1,2,3,\ldots, m-2,$ and the rest $\frac{m (m-1)}{2}-m$ angles $A_{i}OA_{j}=90^{\circ},$ there exists a $PT_{K}(V)$ with $m$ edges, which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Alternative construction of a Fermat coordinate system).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\{ \cos \angle A_{i}O A_{j} \}$ be the cosine matrix of the angles $\angle A_{i} O A_{j},$ for $i,j=1,2,\ldots, m.$
We set $\cos \angle A_{i}OA_{i}=1,$  for $i=1,2,\ldots, m,$ \[\angle A_{j} O A_{j+2}=\angle A_{j+2} O A_{j}=120^{\circ},\] for $j=1,2,3,\ldots, m-2,$ which yields \[\cos \angle A_{j} O A_{j+2}=\cos \angle A_{j+2} O A_{j}=-\frac{1}{2}.\]

We set \[\angle A_{1}O A_{m}=\angle A_{m}OA_{1}=120^{\circ}\] and \[ \angle A_{2}O A_{m-1}=\angle A_{m-1}OA_{2}=120^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{1} O A_{m}=\cos \angle A_{m} O A_{1}=\cos \angle A_{2} O A_{m-1}=\cos \angle A_{m-1} O A_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}.\]

We set the rest $\frac{m(m-1)}{2} - m$ angles \[\angle A_{i} O A_{j} =90^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{i}O A_{j}=0,\] for $i<j.$
Hence, we get \[\angle A_{j} O A_{i} =90^{\circ},\] which yields \[\cos \angle A_{j}O A_{i}=0.\]
By following this construction, we get exactly two elements of the cosine matrix with value $-\frac{1}{2}$ one with value $1$ and the rest with value $0.$
in each row and each column.

These values satisfy the following combinatorial system of equations of unit tangent vectors $e_{i}$ at $O,$ derived by (\ref{eqone}) for $m$ even:

\[-e_{i_{1}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne i_{1} }^{m} e_{i},\]
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}-e_{i_{3}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2},i_{3}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
$\cdots$
\[-e_{i_{1}}-e_{i_{2}}-\ldots-e_{i_{\frac{m}{2}}}=\sum_{i=1, i\ne \{i_{1}, i_{2},i_{3},\ldots, i_{\frac{m}{2}}\} }^{m} e_{i},\]
for $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots, i_{\frac{m}{2}} \in \{1,2,\ldots, m\}.$

label: PTtetrahedron
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{PTtetrahedron}
If $m=4,$ such that: $\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{2}=\angle A_{3}A_{0}A_{4}=90^{\circ}$ and
$\angle A_{2}A_{0}A_{3}=\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{4}=\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{3}=\angle A_{2}A_{0}A_{4}=120^{\circ}$

or $\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{3}=\angle A_{2}A_{0}A_{4}=90^{\circ}$ and
$\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{2}=\angle A_{2}A_{0}A_{3}=\angle A_{3}A_{0}A_{4}=\angle A_{1}A_{0}A_{4}=120^{\circ}$

there exists a $PT_{K}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\})$ with four edges, which form 4 platonic angles with measure $120^{\circ}$
and 2 platonic angles with measure $90^{\circ}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We obtain two different constructions, by applying Theorem~\ref{theorem1} Case (A) and Proposition~\ref{propthree}, for $m=4.$

label: Propfour
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Propfour}
A $PT_{0}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\})$ with one added vertex $O$ cannot be prescribed to a Platonic solid (regular tetrahedron) with vertices $\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3},A_{4}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{3}.$

label: Propfive
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Propfive}
An $APT_{0}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\})$ with one added vertex $O$ and each two edges form a Platonic angle with measure $\arccos{-\frac{1}{3}}$ can be prescribed to a Platonic solid (regular tetrahedron) with vertices $\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3},A_{4}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{3}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By applying the cosine law in $\triangle A_{i}OA_{j}$ and taking into account that $A_{i}A_{j}=1,$ for $i=j=1,2,3,4,$ we obtain that
$A_{i}O=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}.$

label: Prop6
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop6}
A $PT_{0}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\})$ with two added vertices $O$ and $O^{\prime}$ can be prescribed to a Platonic solid (regular tetrahedron) with vertices $\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3},A_{4}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{3}.$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The added vertices $O$ and $O^{\prime}$ are Steiner points having degree three, whose incident edges meet at $120^{\circ}.$
Hence, $MST_{0}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\} )=PT_{0}(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\})$ can be prescribed to a regular (Platonic) tetrahedron $(\{A_{1},A_{2},A_{3,}A_{4}\}.$
head: environment
